biography.plain_text: Robert L. Cadranell is a Pacific Northwest sailor and boatbuilder who worked in the Seattle boatyard and marina industry. Known as Bob, he progressed from junior sailing programmes to offshore racing, competing in Transpac events as skipper and navigator. His practical work included building the Six Metre racer Warhorse at his Lake Union boatyard.

long_biography.plain_text:
Robert L. Cadranell and his wife, Molly, converted a Lake Union marina and repair facility into a moorage for floating homes. The redevelopment required shoreline mitigation as well as planning permission. They removed extensive over-water structures and restored the water's edge with native planting, logs and gravel, improving nearshore habitat for juvenile fish.

Cadranell's competitive record extended beyond ocean passages to the Six Metre class. He rebuilt and modernised racing boats himself, combining workshop skills with experience on the racecourse. In 2009, he finished third in the modern division of the Six Metre World Championship, followed by victory at the North American championship in 2010.
